item.title: Tinubu Returns To Abuja After Umrah In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has returned to Abuja after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia. The President’s aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport at 8:53 p.m. on Wednesday. He was received on arrival by the Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; the Minister of State for Defence; the Inspector-General of Police and other government officials. ﻿ Tinubu departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, at 5:13 p.m. Saudi time after completing the lesser Hajj in Makkah. Before his departure, the President held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. During the visit, Tinubu led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. He was also granted the privilege of entering the Holy Ka’abah on Sunday, where he and members of his delegation performed two raka’at prayers. According to a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President offered prayers for Nigeria’s peace, security, unity and prosperity, as well as divine guidance and wisdom for the country’s leaders. His entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. item.title: Rainbow Coalition: Tinubu tells Nasarawa supporters to vote only APC candidates
item.description: Edwin Philip, Lafia President Bola Tinubu has charged his supporters in Nasarawa State to vote for only the candidates of All Progressives Congress during the forthcoming 2027 general elections. President Tinubu stated this during the APC Presidential Campaign rally which was held on Wednesday in Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital. The president who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima noted that voting candidates of the party would help to sustain the renewed hope agenda of the present administration at all levels of government. According to him, Nasarawa State had witnessed tremendous developments under his watch as President including the construction and rehabilitation of roads, healthcare facilities, schools, among others. Soliciting for the renewal of his mandate come 2027, he appealed to residents of the state to give him another opportunity to lead the country for another four years, by voting for him, promising to do more for the people. “We want to assure you that if God wills and we win the upcoming elections, we will see that we support you for maximum safety. We call on you to vote for all our party’s candidates. The biggest message from the leader of the country is: APC from top to bottom, APC from bottom to top. ​ “We do not want a situation where they say vote for the president and not the governor, or vote for the governor and not the president, or the senator, or the House of Assembly. ​ “We want APC straight! APC straight! APC from top to bottom and bottom to top. May God give us peace and understanding. May God grant us peace of mind. We thank you very much,” he emphasised. He further commended the Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule for embarking on people oriented projects that have transformed the living conditions of the people for the better. On his part, the Chairman of the All Progressives Governors Forum and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodinma highlighted the benefits of the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu, urging the people to ensure that the President returned to power for another four years in order to deliver more dividends of democracy. “It is our decision to continue the deliberate trajectory of Nigeria through the architect of modern Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “We have come to Nasarawa State, we have seen the developments. We have seen that through the Renewed Hope Agenda, the Hope of Nasarawa State is renewed. “And we are here to affirm once more that Nigeria is in good hands, that all of you should vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, “We have worked so hard, we have 31 governors, the party is a family, we plead for peace, we plead for harmony, we plead for a peaceful Nigeria. Support our president, support our governorship candidate, support Nigeria. May God bless all of us as we support the All Progressives Congress,” he said. item.title: 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six years. The singer announced the date in a post on his Instagram handle on Tuesday, describing the project as timeless music. “The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date,” he wrote. View this post on Instagram The announcement comes after months of teasing the album on social media, with 2Baba repeatedly using its title in his Instagram captions. In August, he wrote: “I’ve lived it, I’ve seen it, I’m still here. My new album, Oldest Young Man, soon come.” On his birthday, the singer also described himself as the “forever the oldest young man”. The upcoming project will be his first album since ‘Warriors’, released in 2020, which was his eighth studio album. 2Baba first rose to prominence in the 1990s, composing jingles before co-founding the music group Plantashun Boiz with Blackface and Faze in 1996. He later established himself as one of the pioneers of Afropop, influencing generations of Nigerian artistes with his music. His album releases include ‘Face 2 Face’ (2004), ‘Grass 2 Grace’ (2006), ‘The Unstoppable’ (2009), ‘The Unstoppable International Edition’ (2010), ‘Away and Beyond’ (2012), ‘The Ascension’, ‘Rewind, Select, Update’ (2015) and ‘Warriors’ (2020). item.title: Liverpool collapse to Champions League defeat at Fenerbahce
item.description: Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign. Liverpool had won their opening three European games under Andoni Iraola, but were punished for sloppy defending in a surprise defeat. Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front. But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi’s winner. Fenerbahce’s interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week. The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool’s generosity at the back. Liverpool’s perfect Champions League start allowed Iraola the luxury of leaving out Isak and Florian Wirtz among five changes from Sunday’s 1-0 defeat by Arsenal. Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box. Just four minutes later, though, Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood’s deflected free-kick to equalise. Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark and got an almost immediate reward. Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo’s cross. But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage. Gakpo’s touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post. Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner. Defeat cost Liverpool the chance to move level with Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table as they sit. Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table. item.title: Breaking: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach first U17 Women World Cup final
item.description: Nigeria’s U17 women’s team, the Flamingos, have reached the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup for the first time in history after defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final. The Flamingos secured the historic victory with goals from Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, who scored twice. Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Bashiru extended Nigeria’s lead in the 71st minute. Bashiru completed her brace in the 80th minute to seal Nigeria’s 3-1 victory and book their place in the final. The achievement marks a major milestone for the Nigerian side, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition. The Flamingos will now face Japan in the final as they seek to win their first-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup title. item.title: ‘Hardest days of my life,’ Goalkeeper Owono speaks after Tenerife striker’s death
item.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said Wednesday he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the sickening collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” Spanish police sources told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision. Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend. Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death. “I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Tomas Micha wrote. “We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress. “From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.” Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened. “Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz. “In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.” – Postponements – Earlier it was confirmed Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed. Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca. “After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game… this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes (stadium), has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement. Mallorca said “at times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first”. item.title: Mohbad: DNA samples collected from son, remains
item.description: By Esther Onyegbula LAGOS — The paternity dispute surrounding Master Liam, son of late Nigerian singer Ilerioluwa Oladimeji Aloba, popularly known as Mohbad, has entered a new phase following the collection of DNA samples from the child and the singer’s remains under court supervision. The exercise took place on Saturday, October 31, 2026, following an application by Mohbad’s wife, Omowunmi Aloba, for a court-supervised DNA test to establish Liam’s paternity. The court granted the application and appointed a welfare officer to supervise the exercise, fixing October 31 for the collection of the samples. The paternity question had earlier been raised by Mohbad’s father, Mr Joseph Aloba, who also sought a DNA test to establish whether Liam was the deceased singer’s biological son. Proceedings relating to his request had, however, experienced delays. Security personnel were present during Saturday’s exercise to maintain order. Those in attendance included Mohbad’s mother, Mrs Abosede; his younger brother, Adura; and his wife, Omowunmi. The exercise reportedly became emotional during the identification of the late singer’s remains, which was part of the process. Samples were collected from Mohbad’s remains at Mainland General Hospital, popularly known as the Infectious Diseases Hospital (IDH), Yaba. The samples were subsequently taken to the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre, where Liam’s samples were also collected for forensic examination. Speaking after the exercise, the lawyer representing Omowunmi, Barrister Kabiru, said no date had been fixed for the release of the DNA results. He said the parties would be notified through the court once the results were available. Kabiru also commended the court and the Nigeria Police Force for their professionalism and support in ensuring that the exercise was completed. The DNA test is the latest development in the paternity dispute, which has attracted public attention since Mohbad’s death in September 2023. The results of the forensic examination are expected to provide scientific evidence to assist the court in resolving the paternity question. item.title: Tinubu’s aide highlights ‘technical glitches’ in US election
item.description: President Bola Tinubu’s aide, Tope Ajayi, has highlighted technical glitches and logistical problems that affected the American midterm election, drawing comparisons with criticism of Nigeria’s electoral process. Ajayi, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Publicity, made the remarks in a post on X on Wednesday. He said despite reported problems with the election, political commentators and operatives in the United States had not discredited the process in the same way some Nigerians criticise elections in the country. “I have watched pundits and political operatives and partisan talking heads on various US television networks. Despite some of the technical glitches and logistical problems with the mid-term election they have not discredited the process like many of our people do here,” he wrote. I have watched pundits and political operatives and partisan talking heads on various US television networks. Despite some of the technical glitches and logistical problems with the mid-term election they have not discredited the process like many of our people do here. There… — Temitope Ajayi (@TheTope_Ajayi) November 4, 2026 Ajayi cited reports of ballot scanner programming glitches in parts of New York, equipment malfunction in Broward County, Florida, and ballot shortages in Kansas. He said the equipment malfunction in Broward County delayed the voting process, while a polling station in Kansas reportedly received only 100 paper ballots instead of 100,000. “There was also the case of 250,000 ballots that will be counted manually as a result technical problem with the voting machine,” Ajayi added. His comments come amid lingering controversy over the conduct of Nigeria’s 2023 presidential election, which was criticised by opposition parties and observers over technical and logistical problems. item.title: APC group insists Karimi won Kogi West senatorial primary
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Win With Tinubu (WWT) Grassroots Mobilisation Programme in Kogi State has insisted that Senator Sunday Steve Karimi remains the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Kogi West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, despite a Federal High Court ruling nullifying his candidature. The group said the outcome of the May 18, 2026, APC senatorial primary was reviewed and upheld by the party’s appeal committee, following which Karimi’s name was submitted to and published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as the party’s candidate. It, however, disclosed that Karimi’s legal team had commenced steps to challenge the court ruling at the appellate court. The group’s position was contained in a statement issued on Wednesday by its State Programme Coordinator, Sani Philips, following the judgment delivered by Justice Salim Olasupo Ibrahim in a suit filed by Hon. Samuel Bamidele Aro against Karimi. The group argued that the court ruling should not override the outcome of the party’s internal electoral process, insisting that APC members and delegates in Kogi West had elected Karimi during the primary. It also recalled that controversy had trailed the primary after Aro’s name was allegedly submitted as the winner despite his purported non-participation in the exercise. According to WWT, the party’s appeal committee subsequently reviewed the process and reaffirmed Karimi’s victory. The statement said: “While we note with respect the ruling, we, however, consider it a needless distraction and a deliberate attempt to deny members of the APC in Kogi West the mandate freely given to Senator Sunday Steve Karimi through their votes at the APC Kogi West Senatorial Primaries Election, which took place on May 18, 2026.” The group further questioned aspects of the judgment, alleging that the trial judge departed from established legal principles in reaching his decision. It added that Karimi’s legal team had begun the process of filing an appeal to challenge and set aside the ruling. WWT maintained that Karimi remained the party’s duly nominated candidate pending the determination of the matter by the appellate court. It said: “We wish to affirm that Senator Sunday Steve Karimi remains the authentic, duly nominated and validly elected candidate of our great party for the Kogi West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, pending the determination of the suit at the appellate court.” Recounting the controversy surrounding the primary, the group alleged that Aro’s name had previously been submitted as the winner despite his not participating in the exercise. It said the APC appeal committee intervened, reviewed the process and upheld Karimi’s victory, after which his name was forwarded to INEC and published as the party’s candidate. The mobilisation group also disputed the court’s assessment of the primary, arguing that the ruling did not reflect the process conducted and documented by the relevant organs

item.title: Nigeria’s Foreign Affairs minister appointed Commonwealth CMAG vice-chair
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, has been appointed Vice-Chair of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG), giving the country a leadership role in the organisation’s efforts to uphold democracy, human rights and the rule of law. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the appointment in a statement on Wednesday, saying it was made during the Group’s meeting on the sidelines of the ongoing 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda. The meeting brought together leaders and representatives of the 56 Commonwealth member states, with King Charles III, Head of the Commonwealth, also in attendance. According to the ministry, Odumegwu-Ojukwu’s appointment places Nigeria in a strategic position to contribute to discussions and decisions on democratic governance, institutional accountability and the protection of fundamental rights across member countries. The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group, chaired by Malta’s Chris Fearne, is a rotating body of foreign ministers mandated to uphold the organisation’s fundamental political values, including democracy, human rights, good governance and the rule of law. Established in 1995 under the Millbrook Commonwealth Action Plan, CMAG serves as a mechanism for responding to serious or persistent violations of these shared values by member states. Its responsibilities include assessing political developments in member countries and recommending appropriate collective action where necessary. The group initially focused largely on unconstitutional changes of government, particularly military coups. However, its mandate was expanded by Commonwealth leaders in 2011 to allow more proactive engagement with countries facing threats to democratic governance. Its areas of concern now include unconstitutional changes to political arrangements, suspension of parliaments, electoral irregularities, restrictions on political participation, interference with judicial independence, human rights violations and restrictions on the media and civil society. The ministry said the appointment underscored Nigeria’s continued engagement with the Commonwealth and its commitment to promoting dialogue, cooperation and respect for the shared principles of the 56-member organisation. item.title: Namibia President declares Dangote’s $2.5bn energy investment a landmark for Africa’s industrial future
item.description: …Says project launch most memorable day of her presidency …Unveils 600-million-litre tank farm, 1,700km regional pipeline By Udeme Akpan President of Namibia, Dr Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, has described the $2.5 billion Dangote Namibia Tank Farm and Regional Pipeline Project as a landmark investment that will accelerate Africa’s industrialisation, enhance regional energy security and deepen economic integration across Southern Africa. Speaking at the project’s official launch in Walvis Bay, the Namibian leader praised Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, for demonstrating confidence in Africa’s economic potential through transformative investments in energy infrastructure. She described the occasion as the most memorable day of her presidency. “Today, is the most memorable day of my presidency,” she said, noting that the investment reflects the growing capacity of African entrepreneurs to drive the continent’s transformation. The project comprises a proposed 600-million-litre petroleum storage facility and an approximately 1,700-kilometre regional pipeline network that will position Namibia as a strategic fuel distribution hub for Southern Africa. The infrastructure is expected to improve fuel supply reliability, reduce transportation costs and support economic growth across the region. President Nandi-Ndaitwah said the investment aligns with Namibia’s development priorities and the goals of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), while creating opportunities for employment, skills transfer and industrial expansion. Addressing the ceremony, Aliko Dangote said the investment forms part of the Group’s broader vision to build interconnected centres of production, storage and distribution across Africa. He disclosed that the facility, located near Walvis Bay, will have storage capacity for 360 million litres of diesel and 240 million litres of petrol. The pipeline network will connect Namibia to key markets in Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi and parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo. “We want to invest heavily so that landlocked countries can access petroleum products at cheaper prices,” Dangote said. Dangote also announced that the Group has increased its Africa-wide investment ambition towards 2030 from $50 billion to $60 billion, signalling plans for further expansion across the continent. “What we are launching today represents an investment of $2.5 billion, but Namibia deserves much more. We want to invest more and do more with your government,” he said. Reaffirming his commitment to Africa’s development, Dangote said the continent possesses the resources, talent and markets needed to achieve sustainable industrialisation. “Africa must industrialise Africa,” he declared. item.title: 2027: We won’t endorse any candidate — Health workers
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 elections, the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) on Wednesday declared that its members will not endorse or finance any candidate. The health workers also said they are rejecting a spectator role in the forthcoming elections and demanded binding commitments on CONHESS and outstanding arrears. Speaking in his welcome address at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, the President of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Kabiru Ado Sani, said the union will enter the 2027 general election neither as party loyalists nor as passive observers, but as an organised constituency demanding enforceable commitments on welfare, CONHESS arrears, and outstanding collective agreements. In a strongly worded position ahead of the polls, the union said the question confronting health workers is no longer whether they will participate in the election, but on what terms. “The permutation is now upon us. The question is no longer whether health workers will be in it, but whether we shall be in it as spectators, as foot soldiers, or as a constituency with a strong position,” the MHWUN President said. He warned that health workers must not allow their numerical strength and professional importance to be reduced to election-season mobilisation for politicians who may abandon their concerns afterwards. MHWUN insisted that it remains a trade union, not a political party, and would not endorse any candidate or political platform. “MHWUN is a trade union, not a political party. We will not endorse any party or candidate, and the funds of this Union will not be used to finance any of them,” the union leader stated. He added that members remain free to vote according to their conscience, stressing that no individual has the authority to speak for the union while campaigning for a party. “Our members are free to vote their conscience, and no one speaks for this Union when speaking for a party,” he said. The union argued that its political influence should not depend on telling members whom to vote for, but on forcing every contender for power to confront the health sector’s unresolved demands. “Our influence does not lie in telling members how to vote. It lies in making the health worker’s agenda impossible to ignore, whoever wins,” the MHWUN political head declared. He explained that at the centre of that agenda are the CONHESS salary structure, unpaid arrears, and collective agreements reached with the Federal Government but yet to be fully implemented. The union framed its demands in legal as well as moral terms, insisting that agreements signed by the Federal Government cannot be treated as disposable political promises. “A collective agreement signed by the Federal Government is an obligation of the State,” Dr. Sani said. “It does not lapse when a tenure ends, and no incoming administration is entitled to treat it as the debt of its predecessor.” He wa

item.title: Nigeria can become Africa’s rice export hub — NGF
item.description: …Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has expressed optimism that Nigeria can become a major rice exporter in Africa, insisting that the country’s agricultural potential and available human, financial and natural resources are sufficient to achieve the ambition. The forum said Nigeria could close its 5.3 million metric tonnes rice production deficit and become a net exporter if governments addressed policy inconsistencies, improved agricultural data and provided sustained support to farmers and other players across the value chain. The Director-General of the NGF, Dr. Abdulateef Shittu, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during the launch of the Northwest Rice Diagnostic Report organised by the forum. Shittu said Nigeria currently consumed about 8.6 million metric tonnes of rice annually, a figure projected to rise to 9.1 million metric tonnes next year, while domestic production stood at only 3.3 million metric tonnes. He blamed the production shortfall on inconsistent government policies, poor coordination and other challenges affecting the agricultural sector. According to him, Nigeria has no justification for remaining dependent on imported rice, given its agricultural resources and capacity to supply regional African markets and parts of Europe. He cited China’s transition from food deficit to self-sufficiency through targeted investments, saying Nigeria needed similar political commitment to achieve food security. Shittu said: “You can see the huge gap. So, how do we address this? There are a lot of policy flip-flops, policy mismatch, and quite a number of other challenges that we will all have to address. But my motto simply is that there is no problem without a solution. “We have all the resources, both human and material. We have the land and everything that we need to support farmers and other actors across the value chain. Whatever they need can be guaranteed.” He described credible data as central to agricultural planning and disclosed that the NGF had established a dedicated data department to improve the collection and management of information across states. He urged all 36 states to establish functional Bureaus of Statistics, noting that Kaduna and some other states had already taken the initiative. According to him, national statistics, including Gross Domestic Product figures, should reflect aggregated data from the states and the Federal Capital Territory. The NGF boss said the forum was also challenging figures presented by development partners where it believed they were inaccurate. “If we are saying it is not correct, we have to show them which one is correct,” he said. He added that heads of State Bureaus of Statistics met quarterly under a committee of practice, while commissioners of agriculture also held periodic meetings to exchange ideas and experiences. item.title: Yusuf urges Nigerians to be patient with Tinubu’s policies
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has urged Nigerians to be patient with President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the difficult decisions taken by the administration are aimed at rescuing the economy and stabilising its macroeconomic environment. The governor said the policies had helped stabilise the economy, expressing optimism that the benefits would eventually translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Yusuf, who was represented by Muhammad Yusuf Jamu, spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of campaign coordinators for the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections in Tarauni Local Government Area of Kano State. He said the President had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, adding that economic stability would create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive. “The President’s economic policies have helped rescue the country’s economy and stabilise the macroeconomy. With a stable economy, businesses can go to the markets and carry out their transactions. “We are now at a stage where the economy is growing, and the microeconomy will soon begin to flourish, so that Nigerians can also feel the benefits. “We are in a period where tough decisions have been taken to rescue the country. We urge Nigerians to be patient with the President and his government’s policies. At the end of the day, we will all celebrate,” he said. The governor also urged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano to sustain efforts towards reconciliation and unity within the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: 5 facts to know about Keisha Lance Bottoms, America’s first black female governor
item.description: By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor Her historic victory in Georgia breaks a century-old political barrier for Black women in the United States. The United States has recorded another milestone in its political history following the election of Keisha Lance Bottoms as Georgia’s governor, making her the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican candidate Rick Jackson in the November 3, 2026 gubernatorial election. Her victory is particularly significant in a country where women and Black Americans have historically faced considerable barriers to political representation. Here are five things to know about the woman making history. She is the first Black woman elected governor of a US state Bottoms has broken a significant racial and gender barrier in American politics. Although several women have previously served as governors, no Black woman had ever been elected to lead a US state before her victory in Georgia. Her election represents a landmark moment for Black women in American public life and expands the history of women’s political representation in the country. She will assume office in January 2027. She is also Georgia’s first female governor Beyond making national history as the first Black woman elected governor, Bottoms will also become the first woman to occupy Georgia’s governorship. Her election marks a departure from the state’s political history, in which men have held the office since Georgia became a state. Interestingly, the United States elected its first female governor more than a century ago. Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming became the first woman to take the oath of office as a state governor on January 5, 1925. Ross was elected in November 1924 following the death of her husband, Governor William B. Ross. She subsequently served until January 1927. The distinction is important: Ross made history as the first woman governor, while Bottoms has now made history as the first Black woman elected to the governorship of a US state. She was previously the Mayor of Atlanta Before her historic gubernatorial victory, Bottoms served as Mayor of Atlanta, Georgia’s capital and one of the most prominent cities in the United States. She held the position from 2018 to 2022, becoming a nationally recognised political figure during her tenure. Her mayoral administration coincided with major national developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the protests following the killing of George Floyd in 2020. Her experience in municipal leadership provided a platform for her subsequent return to national politics. She has experience in the White House Bottoms’ political experience extends beyond local government. item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. “I enumerated some of the promises I made to Nigerians. One of the promises is to make sure that security is restored in every part of this country.” ﻿ Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Oborevwori assures residents of peaceful elections
item.description: Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has assured residents of the state of peaceful, free and fair elections. He also warned political parties against violence and urged all to respect the rule of law. Oborevwori gave the assurance at a stakeholders’ meeting on electoral security on Wednesday in Asaba. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the meeting is organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Represented by his Senior Political Adviser, Sen. Emmanuel Aguariavwodo, Oborevwori reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing a conducive political environment for all parties. According to him, all political parties are free to campaign and canvass for votes without intimidation or harassment. The governor also urged political parties to sell their programmes and ideas to the electorate through peaceful campaigns and other lawful engagements. He however, warned that anyone who violated the law would face the consequences, irrespective of political affiliation. Oborevwori while pledging the state government’s support for INEC and its Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, noted that achieving credible elections required collective commitment from all. According to him, this include from the INEC, security agencies, political parties, civil society organisations and the electorate,” he said. He added that no single institution could deliver credible elections independently, urging all stakeholders to collaborate in preventing electoral violence. Also speaking, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Samuel Erale, warned political parties and their supporters against violence, declaring that security agencies were fully prepared to enforce electoral laws. Erale said that the police would monitor political activities and maintain peace before, during and after the elections. “We want to be peaceful. We will be on ground. We will monitor all the activities of everyone,” he said. The CP said security agencies would provide a level playing field for all political parties to exercise their democratic rights within the provisions of the law. He warned that anyone who resorted to violence or breached electoral regulations would face the full weight of the law. “The moment violence is involved, you leave us with no choice than to come and do our duties,” he said. He stressed that maintaining peace, providing a level playing field and ensuring compliance with electoral laws were key priorities of security agencies. He added that no individual, political party or contestant would be exempted from enforcement of electoral laws. Erale also assured stakeholders that security agencies would not compromise their responsibilities, stressing their commitment to credible and transparent elections. He urged political stakeholders to cooperate with security agencies to ensure peaceful campaigns and a violence-free electoral process. item.title: Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, for Abuja after completing his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the holy city of Makkah. According to a statement by the presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s aircraft took off from the Royal Terminal of the airport at exactly 5:13 p.m. Saudi time. Onanuga said the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Consul-General, Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the President to the airport. Before his departure, Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. ﻿ The President had earlier led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers. Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the President offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people. He also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would become a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity. Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport before departing Saudi Arabia. Onanuga said the President’s visit to Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as a renewed commitment to building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation. The statement added that Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers. “President Tinubu left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all,” the statement said. Those in the President’s entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. item.title: How military reduced nationwide attacks by 73 per cent in October as 217 terrorists neutralised
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian military have drastically reduced attacks across various theatres of operations in October 2026, Daily Trust reports. Checks showed that only 98 attacks were recorded during the month under review, representing a 73.3 per cent decline from the 367 attacks recorded in September. A breakdown of the October figures showed that Operation Enduring Peace recorded the highest number of attacks with 29 incidents, followed by Operation Hadin Kai with 27 and Operation Fansan Yamma with 24. Operation Whirl Stroke recorded 12 attacks, while Operation Udo Ka recorded four. Operations Delta Safe and Savannah Shield recorded one attack each. Specifically, the October figure represents a decline of 269 attacks compared with the previous month’s total of 367. This is just as the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, assured Nigerians that the military would intensify efforts to apprehend those responsible for the attacks and bring them to justice. Oluyede also urged troops to remain disciplined, uphold the rules of engagement and respect human rights, while warning against complacency, particularly as the festive season approaches. He called on security agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and joint planning, while urging community leaders and residents to report suspicious activities to security formations or through the military’s toll-free line, 193. Providing updates for Nigerians on military operations across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that many kidnapped victims would continue to be freed from captivity. “During the period under review, the AFN recorded a total of 98 attacks across various theatres of operation. Operation HADIN KAI recorded 27 attacks, Operation FANSAN YAMMA recorded 24, Operation ENDURING PEACE recorded 29, Operation WHIRL STROKE recorded 12, Operation UDO KA (OPUK) recorded 4, while Operation DELTA SAFE and Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD recorded 1 attack each,” the breakdown was contained in a document released on Friday. Earlier in September, Operation Enduring Peace recorded 147 attacks, Operation Fansan Yamma 115, Operation Whirl Stroke 55, Operation Hadin Kai 33, Operation Savannah Shield 13 and Operation Udo Ka four, while Operation Delta Safe recorded none. The senior military officer explained that troops neutralised more than 217 terrorists and criminals, arrested 333 suspects and rescued 349 kidnap victims during the month.
